XIII.}}</noinclude>silence, said, Ye men of Israël, and you that feare God, harken: {{verse|chapter=13|verse=17}}† The God of the people of Israël chose our fathers, and exalted the people vvhen they vvere seiourners in the land of Ægypt, and in a mightie arme brought them out thereof,{{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ ''Exod''.}}∷  {{verse|chapter=13|verse=18}}† and for the space of fourtie yeres tolerated their maners in the desert.{{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ ''Iosue.''}}∷  {{verse|chapter=13|verse=19}}† And destroying seuen nations in the land of Chanaan, by lot he deuided their land among them, {{verse|chapter=13|verse=20}}† as it vvere after foure hundred and fiftie yeres: and after these things he gaue Iudges, vntil Samuël the prophet. {{verse|chapter=13|verse=21}}† And thenceforth they desired a king: and he gaue them {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Iud. 1. Reg. 8.''}}* Saul the sonne of Cis, a man of the tribe of Beniamin, fourtie yeres. {{verse|chapter=13|verse=22}}† and remouing him, he raised them vp {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''1. Reg. 16.''}}* Dauid to be king: to vvhom giuing testimonie, he said, {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Ps. 88, 21.''}}* ''I haue found Dauid the sonne of Iesse, a man according to my hart, vvho shall doe al my vvilles''.

{{verse|chapter=13|verse=23}}† Of his seede God according to his {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Psa. 131, 11.''}}* promisse hath brought forth to Israël a Sauiour {{sc|Iesvs}}, {{verse|chapter=13|verse=24}}† Iohn {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Lu. 3, 3.''}}* preaching before the face of his comming, baptisme of penance to al the people of Israël. {{verse|chapter=13|verse=25}}† And vvhen Iohn fulfilled his course, he said, Vvhom doe {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Lu. 3, 15.''}}* you thinke me to be? I am not he, but behold there commeth after me, vvhose shoes of his feete I am not vvorthie to vnloose.

{{verse|chapter=13|verse=26}}† {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=The Epistle vpõ Tuesday in Easter vveeke.}}Men brethren, children of the stocke of Abraham, & they among you that feare God, to you the vvord of this saluation vvas sent. {{verse|chapter=13|verse=27}}† For they that inhabited Hierusalem, and the princes thereof, not knovving him, nor the voices of the prophets that are read euery Sabboth, iudging haue fulfilled them, {{verse|chapter=13|verse=28}}† and finding no cause of death in him, {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Lu. 23, 1.''}}* desired of Pilate, that they might kil him. {{verse|chapter=13|verse=29}}† And vvhen they had consummated al things that vvere vvritten of him, taking him dovvne from the tree, they put him in a monument. {{verse|chapter=13|verse=30}}† But God raised him vp from the dead the third day: {{verse|chapter=13|verse=31}}† vvho vvas {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Act. 1, 3.''}}* seen for many daies of them that came vp together vvith him from Galilee into Hierusalem, vvho vntil this present are his vvitnesses to the people. {{verse|chapter=13|verse=32}}† And vve preach vnto you that promisse vvhich vvas made to our fathers: {{verse|chapter=13|verse=33}}† that God hath fulfilled this same {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''`to their children'',}}`to our children', raising vp {{sc|Iesvs}}, as in the second Psalme also it is vvritten: ''My sonne art thou, this day haue I begotten thee''.{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Ps. 2, 7.''}} {{verse|chapter=13|verse=34}}† And that he raised him vp from the dead, not to returne novv any more into corruption, thus he said, {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Esa. 55, 3.''}}* ''That I vvil giue you the holy things of Dauid faithful''. {{verse|chapter=13|verse=35}}† And<noinclude>{{rh|||therfore}}</noinclude>
